reason: Read in the directive: the inquiry is set up on the basis of the Tidö agreement and is tasked to "föreslå en ordning där kommuner kan anställa läkare" and to propose measures to make municipal health care more attractive to doctors. That is the inquiry the promise asks for.

Read in the supplementary directive: the inquiry on stronger return work is told to review the rules on inre utlänningskontroller (the grounds for the checks), to decide how digital media may be searched and seized during such checks, and to analyse DNA analyses. Powers to take persons into custody pending an investigation and integrating the checks into the police's ordinary work are not among the tasks, so it covers part of the promise.

Read in the supplementary directive: the inquiry is told to review whether asylum seekers can be made to cover or contribute more to the costs of reception conditions and health care within what EU law allows. That is the subject of the promise, but the directive does not ask for the pros and cons of a fixed fee, so it covers part of it.

Read in the directive: a new inquiry on how the electricity market is developed and regulated, which among other things evaluates the markets for ancillary services and aims to give fossil-free sources and flexible resources market-based payment for the benefits they provide. The promised equal rules for all power sources are not stated as a task, so it covers part of the promise.

Read in the directive: a new system for settlement of certain newly arrived persons that gives municipalities more influence and asks whether a partly different order should decide the distribution of quota refugees (kvotflyktingar). That is the subject of the promise, but agreements between municipalities and Migrationsverket are not a task, so it covers part of the promise.

Read in the supplementary directive: the inquiry on organised crime is told to look at corporate fines for companies used as tools for crime, higher maximum penalties for economic crime and limiting profit from autobiographical accounts of serious crime. These are measures against the income of gangs but not a survey of gang income as a whole, so it covers part of the promise.

Read in the supplementary directive: the inquiry on information exchange with law enforcement is told to propose a new main rule in the secrecy legislation so that authorities can share information to prevent and fight crime. That is one part of the secrecy rules, not a review of all of them, so it covers part of the promise.

Read in the directive: a committee is to produce a basis for decision on full or partial state responsibility for health care, covering all parts of the responsibility including resource allocation and financing. That is a review of organisation and financing of the region-run care, but not of the whole health system, so it covers part of the promise.

Read in the directive: the inquiry is to map and analyse honour-related violence and oppression among children and pupils in preschool, school and after-school care. It is a mapping of how widespread it is, but limited to those settings and not national in scope, so it covers part of the promise.

Read in the directive: one inquiry is to propose a reformed basic protection in the old-age pension system, covering the guarantee pension and the elderly support, with the means testing and the exemption rule for long working lives among its subjects. It is a review of the whole basic protection, not only of its exemption rules, so it covers part of the promise.
